newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS ON COURSE FOR THIRD SUCCESSIVE WORLD MATCHPLAY TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS ON COURSE FOR THIRD SUCCESSIVE WORLD MATCHPLAY TITLE.

text.p: Ernie Els stayed on course for a record-setting third successive World Matchplay title by taking a one-hole lead as Vijay Singh missed three short putts during the first 18 holes of the final on Sunday.
Els lost the first two holes but levelled at the fifth, then went in front at the eighth and remained ahead until the lunch break.

But two ahead playing the 501-yard 18th he could make only par when he hit into a greenside bunker. After what he said was a terrible bunker shot he missed from 10 feet as Singh made a birdie four after reaching the green in two.
The South African defending champion was not entirely happy with his play.
"I am hitting it better but not scoring. Although I am ahead it feels like I am not doing what I should be doing," he said.

Els is making the fifth attempt to win this 33-year-old event three times in succession. Gary Player, Hale Irwin and Seve Ballesteros (twice) have failed to complete hat-tricks on the tough West Course at Wentworth.
Singh drew first blood in the final with a 15-foot birdie putt at the short second and went two ahead with a solid par at the tough 452-yard third as Els took four to get on the green.
But the champion rammed in an eight-footer to win the fourth with a birdie and Singh missed his first short putt, from four feet, at the fifth.
Three holes later Els took the lead, making a birdie from 15 feet, then Singh's three-foot miss at the ninth left him two behind.
Singh got one back at the 11th from seven feet but had to hook a one-iron around the trees as he saved par from a bad drive at the 13th.
Then he missed from five feet at 14 to fall two behind again.
They halved the next three holes in par. Both were fortunate at the 571-yard 17th, Els after hitting a match observer on the head with his drive.
Singh pulled his second shot which struck a branch before bouncing into the greenside rough just off the green. He wasted his good fortune by pitching eight feet short and missing the putt.
"I missed some short putts and I chipped poorly and left everything short," Singh, playing in his first final, said.
